chunks: ‘Ali ibn Muḥammad ibn Ya‘qūb al-Kisā‘ī narrated to me, saying: ‘‘Ali ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl narrated to us from ‘Amr ibn Sa‘īd from Muṣḍiq ibn Ṣadaqah from ‘Ammār ibn Mūsā al-Sābāṭī, who said:

I asked Abā ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) about establishing prayers in the Ḥā’ir. He replied, ‘Prayer is only the obligatory prayer with shortening (Qaṣr), and do not establish the voluntary (Nawāfil) prayers.’

key_terms.الْحَائِرِ: The Ḥā’ir (a specific location associated with Ziyārah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on performing obligatory and voluntary prayers in the Ḥā’ir during Ziyārah?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarah* clarifies the practical jurisprudence of prayer during pilgrimage, distinguishing between the obligatory (Fard) and voluntary (Nawafil) acts. Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) instructs that while the four-rak'ah prayers are shortened to two (Qaṣr) to accommodate the traveler's state, the voluntary prayers are suspended entirely to prevent distraction from the spiritual focus of the Ziyarah. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing ritual obligations with the specific spiritual context of visiting the shrines.
